  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.

  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text">Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitors are LLM-based systems that analyze reasoning traces to detect when outputs may exhibit attributes of interest, such as </span><span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">test-hacking behavior during code generation</span><span id="abstract1.1.3" class="ltx_text">.
In this paper, we use information-theoretic analysis to show that </span><span id="abstract1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">non-zero mutual information between CoT and output is a necessary but not sufficient condition for CoT monitorability.</span><span id="abstract1.1.5" class="ltx_text">
We identify two sources of approximation error that may undermine the performance of CoT monitors in practice: <span id="abstract1.1.5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">information gap</span>, which measures the extent to which the monitor can extract the information available in CoT, and <span id="abstract1.1.5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">elicitation error</span>, which measures the extent to which the monitor approximates the optimal monitoring function.
We further demonstrate that CoT monitorability can be systematically improved through targeted training objectives.
To this end, we propose two complementary approaches: (a) an oracle-based method that directly rewards the monitored model for producing CoTs that maximize monitor accuracy, and (b) a more practical, label-free approach that maximizes conditional mutual information between outputs and CoTs.
Across multiple different environments, we show both methods significantly improve monitor accuracy while preventing CoT degeneration even when training against a monitor, thereby mitigating reward hacking when the task reward is imperfectly specified.</span></p>
  
</div>
<div class="ltx_keywords">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_keywords">Keywords: </h6><span id="id8" class="ltx_text">Machine Learning, ICML</span>
</div><span id="id9" class="ltx_note ltx_role_affiliationnotice"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">affiliationnotice: </span><span id="id9.1" class="ltx_text">Equal contribution</span></span></span></span>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Modern large language models (LLMs) are increasingly trained to generate reasoning traces, also called chain-of-thought (CoT), before producing final outputs.
This capability has enabled the development of CoT monitors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Korbak et al., 2025</a>)</cite>; which are LLM-based systems that analyze these reasoning traces to detect attributes such as <span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">deceptiveness <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">Panfilov et al., 2025</a>)</cite> or misbehaviors during code generation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baker et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stickland &amp; Korbak, 2025</a>)</cite></span>.
However, the practical efficacy of CoT monitoring is undermined by several challenges <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Barez et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, including obfuscation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baker et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, steganographic reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stickland &amp; Korbak, 2025</a>)</cite>, and a general lack of faithfulness in CoT reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Turpin et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lanham et al., 2023</a>)</cite>.
Consequently, our understanding of when, and to what extent, CoT monitors can provide robust supervision remains limited.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This work addresses this gap by establishing the information-theoretic conditions that govern CoT monitorability and demonstrating how to systematically improve it through targeted training. Our contributions include:</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce a formal information-theoretic framework for CoT monitorability and use it to show that necessity of CoT is not a sufficient condition for CoT monitorability, though it can be helpful (Section <a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We identify and formalize two distinct sources of error for practical monitors: information gap (inability to interpret CoT) and elicitation error (inability to simulate the relevant monitoring functionality) (Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Approximate CoT Monitors ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose and empirically validate two complementary training objectives that systematically improve monitorability. We show these methods significantly increase monitor accuracy while preventing CoT obfuscation and reward hacking under optimization pressure (Sections <a href="#S4" title="4 Can CoT Monitorability be Improved? ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> and <a href="#S5" title="5 Experiments and Results ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>).</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>

<span id="S1.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<span id="S1.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S1.I3.i1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">1.</span></span> 
<span id="S1.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S1.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;"> RL training Qwen 7B on difficult math problems from BigMath-RL-Verified. The environment contains a hack, such that negative valued answers always obtain the same task reward as correct answers. During training, a monitor LLM checks the model’s CoT for indicators of hacking. The model, trained to maximize task and monitor reward, learns to fool the monitor by providing genuine-looking CoT but hacky output. Adding our proposed MI-inspired reward term mitigates monitor fooling behaviors, resulting in less hacky models and more transparent CoT. Note that, on this problem, the model gets the answer wrong in its CoT in both settings, because the problem is too hard. This encourages hacking to still receive the task reward. Note also that the true answer is <math id="S1.F1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2^{2/3}-1)^{3}\approx 0.202" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.202</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2^{2/3}-1)^{3}\approx 0.202</annotation></semantics></math>, rather than the <math id="S1.F1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> listed as ground truth in the dataset, further encouraging negative-valued solutions to avoid answer mismatches.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Background &amp; Related Works</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Entropy:</span>
The Shannon entropy of a discrete random variable <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(A)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(A)</annotation></semantics></math>, measures its average uncertainty and is defined as <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="H(A)=-\sum_{a}p(a)\log p(a)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.055em">−</mo><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>a</mi></msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>log</mi><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(A)=-\sum_{a}p(a)\log p(a)</annotation></semantics></math>. The conditional entropy, <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(A\mid B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(A\mid B)</annotation></semantics></math>, measures the remaining uncertainty in <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> after observing <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mutual Information:</span>
The mutual information (MI) between two random variables, <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;B)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;B)</annotation></semantics></math>, quantifies the reduction in uncertainty about one variable from knowing the other. It is defined as:
<math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;B)=H(A)-H(A\mid B)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;B)=H(A)-H(A\mid B).</annotation></semantics></math>
MI is symmetric, so <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;B)=I(B;A)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;B)=I(B;A)</annotation></semantics></math>. A value of <math id="S2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;B)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;B)=0</annotation></semantics></math> implies that the variables are independent. The conditional mutual information, <math id="S2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A;B\mid C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A;B\mid C)</annotation></semantics></math>, measures the MI between <math id="S2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> given a third variable <math id="S2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>. A key identity we will use is the chain rule for mutual information:</p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(A,B;C)=I(A;C)+I(B;C\mid A)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>A</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(A,B;C)=I(A;C)+I(B;C\mid A).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Related Works:</span>
CoT monitoring is a relatively nascent area of research, and its practical utility remains the subject of active debate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Korbak et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Barez et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
To the best of our knowledge, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baker et al. (2025)</a></cite> is the only work that explicitly studies CoT monitoring as a formal problem.
Most prior work has focused on the lack of faithfulness in CoT reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Turpin et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lanham et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Barez et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.
However, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Emmons et al. (2025)</a></cite> argue that for tasks which require CoT, the reasoning tends to be faithful in practice.
Beyond faithfulness, several works explore the possibility of steganography in CoT reasoning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Motwani et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mathew et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stickland &amp; Korbak, 2025</a>)</cite>. That said, current LLMs appear limited in their ability to perform sophisticated steganographic CoT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zolkowski et al., 2025</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Our analysis builds on a growing body of work applying information-theoretic tools to understanding LLMs.
While prior research has used such tools for interpretability and alignment <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al., 2020</a>; <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Belrose et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and others have studied CoT through information gain and information bottleneck principles <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ton et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lei et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, we are the first to use these tools to formalize and study CoT monitorability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For more expanded discussion of related works, please see Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Additional Related Works ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we develop a formal framework to analyze when and why chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning could be monitored effectively.
We begin by formalizing the probabilistic setup and defining key concepts.</p>
</div>

</figure>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We then identify necessary information-theoretic conditions for successful monitoring, showing that the conditional mutual information between CoTs and outputs, <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Z;O|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Z;O|X)</annotation></semantics></math>, plays a critical role in determining monitorability.
Finally, we analyze the gap between ideal (Bayes-optimal) monitors and practical, capacity-bounded monitors, quantifying how decoder limitations affect monitoring performance.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Setup and Definitions</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We model a large language model as a policy, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, that generates text autoregressively.
Our framework focuses on tasks where the model produces a Chain-of-Thought (CoT) before the final output.
More specifically, we assume the directed acyclic graph (DAG)</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\to Z,\qquad(X,Z)\to O,\qquad(X,O)\to Y," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\to Z,\qquad(X,Z)\to O,\qquad(X,O)\to Y,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is the prompt, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> is the chain-of-thought (CoT), <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>O</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O</annotation></semantics></math> is the model’s final action/answer and <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is the attribute of interest that we would like to monitor for.
This structure reflects the typical autoregressive behavior of LLMs: first generating a CoT conditioned on the prompt, and then generating an answer conditioned on both the prompt and the CoT.
We assume that the monitoring target <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is a function of the final output (and possibly the prompt), which aligns with practical applications of monitorability where the goal typically is to predict some aspect of the output.
For example, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baker et al. (2025)</a></cite> used CoT monitoring to detect if generated code was bypassing unit tests.
We present the definitions of the monitors analyzed in this work below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.1</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Output Monitor)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">An output <em id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">monitor</em> is a stochastic mapping <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g:\mathcal{O}\times\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math>; given <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\in\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\in\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, the label is drawn as <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Y\sim g(\cdot\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\sim g(\cdot\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> is the space of prompts, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒪</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{O}</annotation></semantics></math> is the space of model outputs, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math> is the label space, and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math> is the probability simplex over <math id="S3.Thmtheorem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.2</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(CoT Monitor)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Similarly, CoT <em id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">monitor</em> is a stochastic mapping
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒵</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m:\mathcal{Z}\times\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math> with the label drawn as
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Y\,\sim\,m(\,\cdot\mid Z,X)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0.448em" rspace="0.448em">∼</mo><mi>m</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\,\sim\,m(\,\cdot\mid Z,X).</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.3</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Prompt-Only Monitor)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A prompt <em id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">monitor</em> is a stochastic mapping that only uses the prompt <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>:
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p:\mathcal{X}\to\Delta(\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math> with the label <math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> drawn as
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="Y\,\sim\,p(\,\cdot\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0.448em" rspace="0.448em">∼</mo><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\,\sim\,p(\,\cdot\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In our analysis, we focus on two canonical instances of a CoT monitor. The first is the ideal monitor,
which assumes perfect knowledge of the system.
The second instance is the practical or approximate monitor, which is constructed from imperfect approximations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.4</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Bayes-Optimal CoT Monitor)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The <em id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">Bayes-optimal monitor</em>, denoted <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math>, uses the true policy <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> and the true output monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> to compute the ground-truth conditional distribution of the attribute:
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}(Y\mid X,Z):=\mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[g(Y\mid X,o)\big]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}(Y\mid X,Z):=\mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[g(Y\mid X,o)\big].</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.5</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Approximate CoT Monitor)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> be an approximation to the true output distribution <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math> be an approximation to the output monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math>. The predictive distribution of the <em id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">approximate monitor</em>, denoted <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{v}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>q</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{v}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, is defined as
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{v}^{q}(Y\mid X,Z)\;:=\;\mathbb{E}_{\,o\sim q(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[\,v(Y\mid X,o)\,\big]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>q</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.170em">[</mo><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.170em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{v}^{q}(Y\mid X,Z)\;:=\;\mathbb{E}_{\,o\sim q(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[\,v(Y\mid X,o)\,\big].</annotation></semantics></math>
We also write <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{\psi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mi>ψ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{\psi}</annotation></semantics></math> to denote a CoT monitor parameterized by some parameters <math id="S3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ψ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., an LLM).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For prompt-only and output monitors, we can similarly define Bayes-optimal and approximate versions of output and prompt-only monitors. For all monitors, point predictions are attained by taking the <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>argmax</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}</annotation></semantics></math> of their posterior distribution, e.g., <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Y}_{m}(X,Z):=\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\,m(y\mid Z,X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">^</mo></mover><mi>m</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">argmax</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{Y}_{m}(X,Z):=\mathop{\mathrm{argmax}}_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}\,m(y\mid Z,X)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The performance of a monitor is measured by its <span id="S3.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">accuracy</span>, defined as the probability that its point prediction matches the true attribute <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>.
Formally, for a CoT monitor <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>m</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m</annotation></semantics></math>, its accuracy is:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the true data-generating distribution <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(X)\pi(Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(X)\pi(Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math>.
The accuracies for the prompt-only monitor, <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}(p)</annotation></semantics></math>, and the output monitor, <math id="S3.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}(g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}(g)</annotation></semantics></math>, are defined analogously.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Having formally defined the optimal monitors and their accuracies, we can now define the central object of our analysis:
the uplift in monitoring performance that becomes possible when the monitor can observe both the CoT and the prompt.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3.6</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Uplift in CoT monitorability)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For an arbitrary attribute <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>, let the accuracies attained by Bayes-optimal CoT monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Bayes-optimal prompt-only monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>p</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> be <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\text{CoT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">CoT</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\text{CoT}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\text{Prompt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>α</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">Prompt</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\text{Prompt}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then the uplift from monitoring CoT (in addition to monitoring the prompt alone) is <math id="S3.Thmtheorem6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta:=\alpha_{\text{CoT}}-\alpha_{\text{Prompt}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">CoT</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>α</mi><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">Prompt</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta:=\alpha_{\text{CoT}}-\alpha_{\text{Prompt}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Due to space limitations, we omit proofs from the main text, and defer them to the Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Main Proofs and Results ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>, where we also provide some additional results.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we investigate the information-theoretic conditions that govern when and to what extent a CoT provides a meaningful performance uplift. Specifically, we analyze the properties of the policy <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> and the CoT <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math> that allow for a non-trivial monitorability uplift.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Our analysis yields two main insights.
Firstly, we show that the conditional mutual information <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math> provides a strict upper bound on the achievable monitorability uplift.
Secondly, we demonstrate that a CoT being informative about the final output, i.e., <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z|X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z|X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, is a necessary condition for any uplift being possible.
However, it is not a sufficient condition and despite <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z|X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z|X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> there may exist attributes for which monitoring CoT provides no uplift whatsoever.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.7</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Uplift in CoT monitorability depends on conditional MI)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Accuracy uplift <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> in CoT monitorability of an attribute <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> is always non-negative and bounded above by <math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math>. Specifically,
<math id="S3.Thmtheorem7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leq\delta\leq\sqrt{2I(Y;Z|X)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo>≤</mo><msqrt><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>I</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leq\delta\leq\sqrt{2I(Y;Z|X)}</annotation></semantics></math></span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 3.8</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Positivity of MI)

Strictly positive uplift in CoT monitorability requires positive MI, i.e., <math id="S3.Thmtheorem8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0\implies I(Y;Z|X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">⟹</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0\implies I(Y;Z|X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The above results formalize the intuition that the CoT can improve the prediction of an attribute <math id="S3.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> only to the extent that it encodes <span id="S3.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">additional</span> information about this attribute beyond the prompt.
Two important caveats apply:
(1) this result establishes the maximum possible uplift, but does not guarantee that any specific monitor class (e.g., prompted LLMs) will attain it; and
(2) even with high mutual information, a practical monitor may fail if the additional information available in CoT is encoded in ways that resist extraction (e.g., steganographically). We further analyze these limitations in our analysis of practical monitors in Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Approximate CoT Monitors ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We emphasise that the uplift in CoT monitorability is not a static property of a task but intrinsically linked to the policy <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> that generates the CoT.
This has two key implications.
First, the uplifts <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> for two different policies, <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, are not necessarily transferable; a positive uplift under one policy may vanish under another.
Second, and more importantly, this means the uplift is a trainable attribute of the policy itself.
Building on this insight, in Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Can CoT Monitorability be Improved? ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> we introduce training objectives designed to improve the monitorability of CoT.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Do CoTs that matter for the task also help monitoring?</h5>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Emmons et al. (2025)</a></cite> empirically demonstrate that tasks requiring explicit CoT reasoning are more amenable to CoT monitoring.
<span id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
Our theoretical analysis below provides mixed evidence in this regard; necessity of CoT implies <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, which is indeed a necessary condition for CoT monitorability. However, this is not a sufficient condition for CoT monitorability.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem9" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem9.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.9</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem9.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(MI decomposition)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem9.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S3.Thmtheorem9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=g(O,X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=g(O,X)</annotation></semantics></math> for the stochastic map <math id="S3.Thmtheorem9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g:\mathcal{\mathcal{}}O\times\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g:\mathcal{\mathcal{}}O\times\mathcal{X}\to\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then</span></p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)\ =\ I(Y;Z\mid X)\ +\ I(O;Z\mid Y,X)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.778em">=</mo><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo rspace="0.500em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.722em">+</mo><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)\ =\ I(Y;Z\mid X)\ +\ I(O;Z\mid Y,X).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 3.10</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem10.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<span id="S3.Thmtheorem10.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Non-zero MI between CoT and output is a necessary but not sufficient condition for monitorability</span>)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem10.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Assume <math id="S3.Thmtheorem10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y=g(O,X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y=g(O,X)</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g:\mathcal{\mathcal{}}O\times\mathcal{X}\!\to\!\mathcal{Y}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.108em" rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">→</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g:\mathcal{\mathcal{}}O\times\mathcal{X}\!\to\!\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math> is a stochastic map.</span></p>
<ol id="S3.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Necessity) For any attribute </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, strictly positive uplift in CoT monitorability (i.e., </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">) requires </span><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">(Not sufficiency) </span><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> does </span><em id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_emph">not</em><span id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> guarantee a strictly positive uplift in CoT monitorability.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 3.11</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Necessity of CoT reasoning fulfills the necessary condition for CoT monitorability)<span id="S3.Thmtheorem11.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The necessary condition for CoT monitorability, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z|X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z|X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, is implied by CoT being necessary for solving the task. However, <math id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z|X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z|X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> can also be fulfilled in other cases, such as when CoT is a <em id="S3.Thmtheorem11.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">post-hoc explanation</em> of the model output or when CoT contains excerpts of the output.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Approximate CoT Monitors</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The analysis in the previous section considers a Bayes–optimal CoT monitor that, by definition, has two key advantages over any practical monitor.
First, it assumes perfect information, including access to both the true output distribution—the model’s conditional <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math>—and the true output monitor <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Second, it assumes unlimited capacity and computation, allowing it to perfectly represent the ground–truth conditional
<math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}(Y\mid X,Z)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[g(Y\mid X,o)\big]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">[</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>o</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}(Y\mid X,Z)\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{o\sim\pi(O\mid X,Z)}\!\big[g(Y\mid X,o)\big]</annotation></semantics></math>.
In practice, however, any real-world monitor can not be presumed to have access to these distributions.
Such a monitor, then, would necessarily underperform the Bayes-optimal monitor.
Our goal in this section is to quantify the performance gap between a practical, approximate monitor <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{v}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>q</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{v}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Bayes-optimal monitor <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> (c.f. Definitions <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem4" title="Definition 3.4 (Bayes-Optimal CoT Monitor). ‣ 3.1 Setup and Definitions ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> and <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem5" title="Definition 3.5 (Approximate CoT Monitor). ‣ 3.1 Setup and Definitions ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>).
We begin by bounding the degradation in predictive accuracy and then trace this gap back to two distinct sources of error: a failure of the CoT monitor to model the agent’s policy and a failure to model the output monitor function <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>O</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math> well.
In the results presented below, we would abuse notation by using the shorthand <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> to denote the true data-generating distribution <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(Z|X)p(X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(Z|X)p(X)</annotation></semantics></math> and use <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(O,X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(O,X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> to denote the distribution <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(O|Z,X)\pi(Z|X)p(X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mrow><mi>Z</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Z</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(O|Z,X)\pi(Z|X)p(X)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lemma">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 3.12</span></span><span id="S3.Thmtheorem12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">[Accuracy bound for approximate monitor]
The difference in accuracy between the approximate monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{v}^{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>v</mi><mi>q</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{v}^{q}</annotation></semantics></math> and the Bayes-optimal monitor <math id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> is bounded by:</span></p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}(q,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>spec</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}(q,v)</annotation></semantics></math> is the <em id="S3.Thmtheorem12.p1.2.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">misspecification error</em>, defined as the expected KL-divergence between the ideal and approximate posterior distributions:</span></p>

</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This lemma establishes that the degradation in monitor accuracy is controlled by the misspecification error <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>spec</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In the following proposition, we show that we can decompose the misspecification error into two error terms.</p>
</div>

<div id="S3.Thmtheorem13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.Thmtheorem13.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S3.Thmtheorem13.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The misspecification error is bounded by the sum of the errors in the approximate components:</span></p>
