<div id="A5.7" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A5.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><em id="A5.p9.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Necessity:</em><span id="A5.p9.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> As it is given that <math id="A5.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">δ</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, by Corollary <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem8" title="Corollary 3.8. ‣ 3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.8</span></a>, we have <math id="A5.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. From Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem9" title="Lemma 3.9 (MI decomposition). ‣ Do CoTs that matter for the task also help monitoring? ‣ 3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.9</span></a> we have <math id="A5.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)\geq I(Y;Z\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)\geq I(Y;Z\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A5.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;0\Rightarrow I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;0\Rightarrow I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. 
<br class="ltx_break"><em id="A5.p9.1.2.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Not Sufficiency:</em> By Lemma <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem9" title="Lemma 3.9 (MI decomposition). ‣ Do CoTs that matter for the task also help monitoring? ‣ 3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.9</span></a>, we have
<math id="A5.p9.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)\;=\;I(Y;Z\mid X)\;+\;I(O;Z\mid Y,X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.280em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.502em">+</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)\;=\;I(Y;Z\mid X)\;+\;I(O;Z\mid Y,X)</annotation></semantics></math>. 
<br class="ltx_break">Because both terms on RHS are nonnegative,
<math id="A5.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> only requires that at least one term is strictly positive.
Thus, let <math id="A5.p9.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(O;Z\mid Y,X)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid Y,X)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> while <math id="A5.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z\mid X)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z\mid X)=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="A5.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z\mid X)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z\mid X)=0</annotation></semantics></math>, then by Proposition <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem7" title="Proposition 3.7 (Uplift in CoT monitorability depends on conditional MI). ‣ 3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.7</span></a>, we have <math id="A5.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">δ</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=0</annotation></semantics></math>, i.e., no uplift in CoT monitorability.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<p id="A5.p11.7" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p11.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Since the square root function is concave, we can apply Jensen’s inequality to move the expectation inside the square root:</span></p>

<p id="A5.p11.8" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p11.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">By definition, the term inside the square root is the misspecification error, <math id="A5.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}(q,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">ϵ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">spec</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{\mathrm{spec}}(q,v)</annotation></semantics></math>. <p id="A5.p11.9" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p11.9.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Finally, by definition, the Bayes-optimal monitor <math id="A5.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> has the maximum possible accuracy, so <math id="A5.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}(m_{g}^{\pi})\geq\mathrm{Acc}(m_{v}^{q})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Acc</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi></msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}(m_{g}^{\pi})\geq\mathrm{Acc}(m_{v}^{q})</annotation></semantics></math>. This means their difference is non-negative, and the bound holds for the absolute value, completing the proof.
∎</span></p>

<p id="A5.p15.5" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.p15.5.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This pointwise inequality holds for all <math id="A5.p15.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,z)</annotation></semantics></math> in the support of <math id="A5.p15.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math>. Since the KL divergence is non-negative, we can take the expectation over <math id="A5.p15.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,Z)\sim\pi(X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">∼</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,Z)\sim\pi(X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math> on both sides, and the inequality is preserved. This yields the final result:</span></p>

X,O)\big)\big].\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">E.1 </span>Practical CoT-Monitors Can Outperform Practical Output Monitors</h3>

<div id="A5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In Section </span><span class="ltx_ref ltx_missing_label ltx_ref_self" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"></span><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, we discussed how the comparative performance of CoT monitors relative to output monitors can be better in practice due to CoTs having higher </span><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">usable</span><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> information, despite generally having lower </span><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Shannon</span><span id="A5.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> information.
In this appendix, we expand on that discussion further.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A5.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition E.2</span></span><span id="A5.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Practical output monitor)<span id="A5.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let <math id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the Bayes–optimal output monitor.
A <em id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">practical output monitor</em> is any conditional predictor
<math id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w:\,(X,O)\mapsto\Delta(\mathcal{Y})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">w</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.278em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.448em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒴</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w:\,(X,O)\mapsto\Delta(\mathcal{Y})</annotation></semantics></math>
with probabilities <math id="A5.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w(Y\mid X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">w</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w(Y\mid X,O)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Higher <math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>-Information in CoT:</h5>

<div id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Shannon information does not distinguish between the relative ease of the extractability of the computation.
An alternative notion of information, which accounts for practical limitations of predictors, is </span><math id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">-Information  </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al. (2020)</a></cite><span id="A5.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition E.3</span></span><span id="A5.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Conditional predictive <math id="A5.Thmtheorem3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>-information)<span id="A5.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A5.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let <math id="A5.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> denote a hypothesis class for monitors under a proper scoring rule <math id="A5.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math>. <div id="A5.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark E.4</span></span><span id="A5.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Computation can increase usable information)<span id="A5.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Unlike Shannon mutual information, <math id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\mathcal{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\mathcal{V}}</annotation></semantics></math> does <em id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">not</em> obey a data-processing inequality in general.
A computed representation <math id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z=T(X,O)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z=T(X,O)</annotation></semantics></math> may yield <math id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\mathcal{V}}(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;I_{\mathcal{V}}(Y;O\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\mathcal{V}}(Y;Z\mid X)&gt;I_{\mathcal{V}}(Y;O\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math> because <math id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> can expose features that are easier for <math id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> to exploit.
See <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">Xu et al. (2020)</a></cite> for exposition of the idea that computation can create <em id="A5.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1.2" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">usable</em> information for constrained observers.</span></p>
</div>
</div>

<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Additional Theoretical Results</h2>

<section id="A6.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.1 </span>Lower Bound on <math id="A6.SS1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math> for Desired Monitor Accuracy</h3>

<div id="A6.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In Section </span><a href="#S3.SS2" title="3.2 Necessary Conditions for Uplift in CoT Monitorability ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> of the main text, we established an upper bound on the monitorability uplift (</span><math id="A6.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">), linking it directly to the conditional mutual information </span><math id="A6.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
This appendix offers a complementary perspective on the relation between CoT monitor performance and </span><math id="A6.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> by using Fano’s Inequality to derive a different type of necessary condition.
Specifically, instead of bounding the </span><em id="A6.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">uplift</em><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, the following proof establishes a </span><em id="A6.SS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">minimum required mutual information</em><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to achieve a target monitor accuracy </span><math id="A6.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\text{CoT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">CoT</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\text{CoT}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
This bound provides an insight about the magnitude of </span><math id="A6.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p1.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> required for achieving a certain level of monitor accuracy.</span></p>
</div>

Let <math id="A6.Thmtheorem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Z,X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" <div id="A6.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition F.2</span></span><span id="A6.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Necessary MI Threshold for <math id="A6.Thmtheorem2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha_{\text{CoT}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">CoT</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{\text{CoT}}</annotation></semantics></math>-Accurate CoT Monitor)<span id="A6.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A6.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let <math id="A6.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" <div id="A6.SS1.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A6.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let the MAP estimator of <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math> be <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{Y}_{m_{g}^{\pi}}(X,Z)=\arg\max_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}m_{g}^{\pi}(y|X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">max</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">∈</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic" mathcolor="#000000">𝒴</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi We are given that the accuracy of this estimator is <math id="A6.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="A6.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">We can now apply Fano’s Inequality (Lemma <a href="#A6.Thmtheorem1" title="Lemma F.1 (Fano’s Inequality). ‣ F.1 Lower Bound on 𝐼(𝑌;𝑍|𝑋) for Desired Monitor Accuracy ‣ Appendix F Additional Theoretical Results ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.1</span></a>) to this optimal estimator.

stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" <div id="A6.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark F.3</span></span><span id="A6.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A6.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The bound given in Proposition <a href="#A6.Thmtheorem2" title='Proposition F.2 (Necessary MI Threshold for 𝛼_"CoT"-Accurate CoT Monitor). ‣ F.1 Lower Bound on 𝐼(𝑌;𝑍|𝑋) for Desired Monitor Accuracy ‣ Appendix F Additional Theoretical Results ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory' class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F.2</span></a> is not vacuous only if <math id="A6.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\pi}(Y\mid X)&gt;T_{\alpha}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">H</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">α</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\pi}(Y\mid X)&gt;T_{\alpha}</annotation></semantics></math>, or equivalently, if we have positive uplift (<math id="A6.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">δ</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">&gt;</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A6.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The proposition dictates that for a fixed initial uncertainty, </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\pi}(Y|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">H</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\pi}(Y|X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, there is a minimum amount of information a CoT must provide to achieve a desired accuracy.
To gain intuition for this proposition, we can calibrate it for a challenging binary task where </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">κ</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa=2</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{\pi}(Y|X)\approx 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">H</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≈</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{\pi}(Y|X)\approx 1</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> bit.
To achieve a moderate accuracy of </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="70\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">70</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">70\%</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, we only require the CoT to supply at least </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\pi}(Y;Z|X)\geq 1-0.881=0.119" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.881</mn></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.119</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\pi}(Y;Z|X)\geq 1-0.881=0.119</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> bits.
However, as we move towards higher reliability, the informational cost increases dramatically. For instance, reaching </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">90</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90\%</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> accuracy requires the mutual information to be at least </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.531" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.531</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.531</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> bits—a disproportionately large increase for the next 20-point gain.
Pushing for </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="99\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">99</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">99\%</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> accuracy is even more demanding, requiring MI </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(Y;Z|X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z|X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to increase by </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">80</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80\%</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to at least </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.919" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0.919</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.919</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> bits for the final 9-point improvement. This effect occurs because the relationship between accuracy and this information cost is strongly super-linear.
This is a direct consequence of the shape of the binary entropy function, </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{b}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">h</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{b}(p)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> which has an upside-down ‘U‘ shape and becomes extremely steep as </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.14" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> approaches </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.15" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> or </span><math id="A6.SS1.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS1.p4.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.2 </span>Performance Gap Between an Action Monitor and the Bayes-Optimal CoT Monitor</h3>

<div id="A6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In our work, we posit output monitor </span><math id="A6.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(o,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(o,x)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> as the oracle, while Bayes-optimal CoT monitor </span><math id="A6.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{g}^{\pi}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{g}^{\pi}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> provides us with an upper bound on how well any CoT monitor could perform.
The two objects are quite similar, with the only advantage of the output monitor being that it observes the realized output, while even the Bayes-optimal CoT monitor is forced to average over all possible outputs.
In the following proposition, we bound the performance gap between these two monitors.</span></p>
</div>

<p id="A6.Thmtheorem4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Then the gap in their accuracy is bounded by:</span></p>

X,Z)\,}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.778em" mathcolor="#000000">Acc</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">CoT</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">⋆</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.778em">≤</mo><msqrt style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"> 2</mn><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\ \leq\ \mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{\mathrm{Act}}-\mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{\mathrm{CoT}}\leq\ \sqrt{\,2\,I(Y;O\mid X,Z)\,}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>

<div id="A6.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Proof.</h6>
<div id="A6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Lower bound:<span id="A6.SS2.p2.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">
We start by expanding the difference in accuracies. Note that the expectation for <math id="A6.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{\mathrm{Act}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Acc</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Act</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">⋆</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{\mathrm{Act}}</annotation></semantics></math> can be written as an iterated expectation.</span></span></p>

<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Interpretation of the Performance Gap.</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The proposition shows that the performance gap between an action monitor and a CoT monitor is governed by </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
This term measures how much information the action </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> provides about the attribute </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> that was not already available in the prompt </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and CoT </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
Note that </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is upper-bounded by the minimum of the two relevant conditional entropies:</span></p>
<table id="A6.Ex87" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Thus, for </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to be large, two conditions must </span><em id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">both</em><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> be met:</span></p>
<ol id="A6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">

<li id="A6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The first condition is fundamentally a property of the </span><em <div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The second condition is intrinsic to the </span><em Equivalently, it is about the </span><em id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.9" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">label sensitivity</em><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> of outputs, not the stochasticity of the policy.
In practice this has two complementary effects:
firstly, stronger </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="O\!\mapsto\!Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.108em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.108em" stretchy="false">↦</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">O\!\mapsto\!Y</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> dependence enlarges the information </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> that is exclusively only available to the action monitor.
Secondly, such a </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is likely to be more complex and non-linear, making it </span><em id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.14" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">harder to approximate</em><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p3.1.15" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, increasing elicitation error in practical monitors.</span></p>
