<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A6.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Low Output Uncertainty, Low Label Sensitivity <math id="A6.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Small <math id="A6.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This is the ideal regime for CoT monitoring: policy </span><math id="A6.I2.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> generates highly informative CoT </span><math id="A6.I2.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.I2.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">
and the attribute being monitored is coarse-grained (e.g., “is the output likely to contain any code snippets or not?").</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Low Output Uncertainty, High Label Sensitivity <math id="A6.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Small <math id="A6.I2.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A6.I2.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This is the scenario in which, even though the attribute being monitored is somewhat fine-grained (e.g., “is the output code being generated going to use a specific external library or not?"), the policy compensates for this by being more transparent and giving more of the attribute relevant details in its CoT (e.g., the model’s CoT explicitly states what external libraries it will use in its code output).</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">High Output Uncertainty, Low Label Sensitivity <math id="A6.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Small <math id="A6.I2.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This is in some sense, the inverse of the previous case.
Here, the policy has high residual uncertainty over its outputs (potentially because CoT is not sufficiently detailed). However, </span><math id="A6.I2.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O|X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="false" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O|X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.I2.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> remains small, because the attribute being monitored is sufficiently coarse that very little information is required to determine it.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="A6.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A6.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">High Output Uncertainty, High Label Sensitivity <math id="A6.I2.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Rightarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">⇒</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Rightarrow</annotation></semantics></math> Large <math id="A6.I2.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;O\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;O\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math></span><span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. </span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="A6.I2.i4.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This is the most challenging regime for CoT monitorability, resulting in the largest performance gap.
Here, the policy generates a high-level CoT that leaves critical implementation choices unresolved, while the attribute is highly sensitive to how those choices are realized.
For example, a CoT may perfectly describe a correct recursive algorithm, while the critical attribute “does the code cause a stack overflow?" is determined entirely by a post-CoT implementation choice, such as passing a large matrix by value.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Which attributes are more CoT-monitorable?</h5>

<div id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This analysis suggests that attributes are easier to monitor from a CoT when the CoT itself pins down the attribute (</span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H(Y\mid X,Z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H(Y\mid X,Z)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is small).
This is typical for coarse, plan-level properties that are likely to occur in </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. Hhowever, it is less likely to be true for low-level details that LLMs may not verbalize in their CoT.
A corollary of this fact is that LLMs should be trained to verbalize the aspects outputs problems that we would like to monitor in their CoT.
Our proposed method of maximizing </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> achieves this by improving quality of CoT in an attribute-agnostic way. However, this does not provide guarantees on whether verbalization of some specific attribute of interest, </span><math id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, improves or not.
Thus, we believe that there is room for developing more targeted interventions that elicit verbalization specific to high-value attributes of interest.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.3 </span>Misspecification Error Specific to CoT</h3>

<div id="A6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In Proposition </span><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem13" title="Proposition 3.13 (Decomposition of Misspecification Error). ‣ 3.3 Approximate CoT Monitors ‣ 3 Information-Theoretic Analysis of CoT monitorability ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.13</span></a><span id="A6.SS3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, we showed that a practical monitor’s performance gap decomposes into an information gap and an elicitation error. That analysis, however, measured the total performance gap. Here, we refine this by isolating the error component specifically attributable to the CoT. We define the marginal misspecification error as the difference between the misspecification at the CoT level and at the prompt level. The following proposition formalizes this quantity as </span><math id="A6.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">info</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and shows it corresponds to the net loss in conditional mutual information captured by the practical monitor.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A6.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition F.5</span></span><span id="A6.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Marginal misspecification error)<span id="A6.Thmtheorem5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A6.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let
<math id="A6.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v):=I(Y;Z\mid X)-I_{m_{v}^{q}}(Y;Z\mid X)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">info</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">−</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v):=I(Y;Z\mid X)-I_{m_{v}^{q}}(Y;Z\mid X).</annotation></semantics></math> be the performance gap between the practical and the idealized monitor at CoT level, then</span></p>
<ol id="A6.I3" class="ltx_enumerate ltx_leftmargin_flush">
<li id="A6.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A6.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A6.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v)=\mathbb{E}_{\pi(X,Z)}\big[\mathrm{KL}(m_{g}^{\pi}(\cdot|X,Z)\,\|\,m_{v}^{q}(\cdot|X,Z))\big]-\mathbb{E}_{\pi(X)}\big[\mathrm{KL}(m_{g}^{\pi}(\cdot|X)\,\|\,m_{v}^{q}(\cdot|X))\big]." rspace="0.280em">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝔼</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mpadded style="width:1.431em;" width="1.431em"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">KL</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0.170em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.337em">∥</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">m</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\pi(X)}\mathrm{KL}\!\big(\pi(Y\mid X)\,\|\,m(Y\mid X)\big)\;\leq\;\mathbb{E}_{\pi(X,Z)}\mathrm{KL}\!\big(\pi(Y\mid X,Z)\,\|\,m(Y\mid X,Z)\big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS3.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS3.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">hence <math id="A6.SS3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">info</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">v</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≥</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{info}}(q,v)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which is item (ii).
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">F.4 </span>Performance Gap Between Activation Monitor and CoT Monitor</h3>

<div id="A6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In the main text, our analysis is based on a simplified DAG where the model’s reasoning is represented by a single trace, </span><math id="A6.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS4.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">:</span></p>

<p id="A6.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS4.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For this appendix, we extend this model to better reflect the internal workings of a language model, by splitting </span><math id="A6.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A6.SS4.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> into two distinct channels:</span></p>
<ol id="A6.I4" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A6.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span>

<p id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">A textual Chain-of-Thought (<math id="A6.I4.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Z_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Z_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>)</span><span id="A6.I4.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, which is the explicit, verbalized reasoning.</span></p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition F.6</span></span><span id="A6.Thmtheorem6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Performance gap between Bayes-optimal Activation and CoT monitors)<span id="A6.Thmtheorem6.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A6.Thmtheorem6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.Thmtheorem6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.Thmtheorem6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let the Bayes-optimal accuracies for the CoT monitor and the activation monitor be:</span></p>

mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em" rspace="0.280em">]</mo></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><munder><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">max</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi></munder><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathcolor="#000000">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{z_{L}\sim\pi(\cdot\mid x,z_{T})}\big[\max_{y}p(y\mid x,z_{T},z_{L})\big]\;\geq\;\max_{y}\,\mathbb{E}_{z_{L}\sim\pi(\cdot\mid x,z_{T})}\big[p(y\mid x,z_{T},z_{L})\big]\;=\;\max_{y}p(y\mid x,z_{T}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A6.SS4.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A6.SS4.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The term inside the outer expectation is therefore non-negative for all <math id="A6.SS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,z_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,z_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>, proving the lower bound.</span></p>
</div>

The term inside the square root is precisely the definition of the conditional mutual information <math id="A6.SS4.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(Y;Z_{L}\mid X,Z_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(Y;Z_{L}\mid X,Z_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. This yields the final upper bound:</span></p>

style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">⋆</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.558em">≤</mo><msqrt style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mrow><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"> 2</mn><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">L</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">T</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msqrt></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" class="ltx_mathvariant_italic" lspace="0.0835em" mathcolor="#000000" mathvariant="italic" separator="true">∎</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{T,L}-\mathrm{Acc}^{\star}_{T}\;\leq\;\sqrt{\,2\,I(Y;Z_{L}\mid X,Z_{T})\,}.\qed</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Analysis of the Mutual Information Reward</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In Section </span><a href="#S4.SS2.SSS1" title="4.2.1 Estimation and Practical Optimization of 𝐼(𝑂;𝑍∣𝑋) ‣ 4.2 A Label-Free Proxy: Maximizing 𝐼(𝑂;𝑍∣𝑋) ‣ 4 Can CoT Monitorability be Improved? ‣ Analyzing and Improving Chain-of-Thought Monitorability Through Information Theory" class="ltx_ref" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2.1</span></a><span id="A7.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, we introduced a practical, per-rollout estimator for the conditional mutual information </span><math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to serve as a reward signal.
In this appendix, we provide further analysis of this estimator by connecting it to the highly influential InfoNCE objective </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A7.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oord et al., 2018</a><span id="A7.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A7.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, and discuss its statistical properties.</span></p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">G.1 </span>A Primer on InfoNCE</h3>

<div id="A7.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">InfoNCE is a general method for estimating log density ratios of the form </span><math id="A7.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log\frac{p(y|x)}{q(y)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log\frac{p(y|x)}{q(y)}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> using contrastive learning </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Oord et al., 2018</a><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
InfoNCE works by training a critic function </span><math id="A7.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to distinguish ‘positive‘ samples drawn from the target conditional distribution </span><math id="A7.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y|x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y|x)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> from ‘negative‘ samples drawn from a noise distribution </span><math id="A7.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">For the specific task of estimating mutual information, InfoNCE is configured to target the density ratio that appears in the definition of MI, </span><math id="A7.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(X;Y)=\mathbb{E}_{p(x,y)}[\log\frac{p(y|x)}{p(y)}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝔼</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(X;Y)=\mathbb{E}_{p(x,y)}[\log\frac{p(y|x)}{p(y)}]</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">. This is achieved by setting the noise distribution </span><math id="A7.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q(y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> to be the marginal distribution </span><math id="A7.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Given a batch of </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(x_{i},y_{i})\}_{i=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> drawn from the joint distribution </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, InfoNCE provides a lower bound on the mutual information </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.5" class="ltx_text" id="A7.SS1.p3.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
For a single anchor </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{i}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, the objective contrasts its corresponding positive sample </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{i}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> with all other samples </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{y_{j}\}_{j=1}^{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">K</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{y_{j}\}_{j=1}^{K}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> in the batch, which serve as negatives.
The resulting MI estimator </span><math id="A7.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{\text{NCE}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">NCE</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{\text{NCE}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is given below </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(for derivation, see </span><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Poole et al., 2019</a><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.15" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, Section 2.3)</span></cite><span id="A7.SS1.p3.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>

style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mfrac style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000"><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">K</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">∑</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">=</mo><mn style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">1</mn></mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">K</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">exp</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000">.</mo></mrow><annotation p(x,y)}\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{i=1}^{K}\log\frac{\exp\{f(x_{i},y_{i})\}}{\frac{1}{K}\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp\{f(x_{i},y_{j})\}}\right]\leq I(X;Y).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A7.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">where </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is the critic.
Though </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> can be any function,
the optimal critic is </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\log p(y|x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">|</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\log p(y|x)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Poole et al., 2019</a><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.7" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
This objective turns MI estimation into a contrastive learning task: the critic is trained to assign high scores to positive pairs </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{i},y_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{i},y_{i})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and low scores to negative pairs </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x_{i},y_{j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">y</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x_{i},y_{j})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> for </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\neq i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">j</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≠</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\neq i</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.11" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
In our work, we use the conditional version of this objective to target </span><math id="A7.SS1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I(O;Z\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(O;Z\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.SS1.p4.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">

<div id="A7.Thmtheorem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A7.Thmtheorem1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition G.1</span></span><span id="A7.Thmtheorem1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Equivalence to Conditional InfoNCE)<span id="A7.Thmtheorem1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A7.Thmtheorem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.Thmtheorem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.Thmtheorem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Let the critic be the log-likelihood of the policy, <math id="A7.Thmtheorem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{\theta}(o,z;x):=\log\pi_{\theta}(o\mid z,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">f</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">π</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">θ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">o</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">z</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">,</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">x</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{\theta}(o,z;x):=\log\pi_{\theta}(o\mid z,x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Our estimator <math id="A7.Thmtheorem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{I}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">^</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{I}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the sample value of the logarithm of the conditional InfoNCE objective.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.2" class="ltx_proof">

∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A7.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">This direct equivalence allows us to infer several important properties of our MI reward signal.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A7.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A7.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary G.2</span></span><span id="A7.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Lower Bound on MI)<span id="A7.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A7.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A7.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">The expected value of our estimator is a lower bound on the true conditional mutual information: <math id="A7.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}[\hat{I}_{i}]\leq I(O;Z\mid X)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">^</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">≤</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">O</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">;</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">Z</mi></mrow><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" fence="true" lspace="0em" mathcolor="#000000" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">X</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}[\hat{I}_{i}]\leq I(O;Z\mid X)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A7.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A7.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary G.3</span></span><span id="A7.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Bias and Variance)<span id="A7.Thmtheorem3.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A7.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="A7.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{I}_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">I</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">^</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;" mathcolor="#000000">i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{I}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="A7.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> is high-bias, but low variance estimator:</span></p>
<ol id="A7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">

<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Additional Related Works</h2>

<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">CoT Monitoring, Faithfulness, and Obfuscation:</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring has been proposed as a valuable, but, a fragile, opportunity for model oversight </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Korbak et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
Number of recent works in AI safety use CoT inspection to detect misbehaviors in LLMs </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Scheurer et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Greenblatt et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meinke et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
The primary challenge, identified by </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Baker et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, is that if any optimization pressure based on feedback from CoT monitor gets applied to CoT, CoT monitors’ performance can degrade heavily.
This practical risk is compounded by the fundamental problem of CoT faithfulness: a model’s stated reasoning may be a plausible but misleading rationalization of a biased answer, rather than a reflection of its actual computational process </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">Turpin et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lanham et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arcuschin et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
Furthermore, models may learn to circumvent CoT monitors by using steganography to hide their reasoning.
While several works have provided circumstantial evidence of steganographic reasoning in LLMs </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Farquhar et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Motwani et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Mathew et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zolkowski et al., 2025</a>; <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Skaf et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">,
on the whole, current LLMs seem to lack the ability to reliably and consistently use steganographic reasoning.
For models that can perform steganographic reasoning, </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Stickland &amp; Korbak (2025)</a></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1.24" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> explore generator-to-monitor transferability and find that self-monitoring is optimal in that case.
This empirical finding is also confirmed by our work.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Improving Faithfulness of CoT:</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Our focus on improving ‘monitorability’ of CoT is similar in spirit to various other works that aim to improve faithfulness of CoT.
Key strategies include enforcing faithfulness by construction by prompting models to generate executable code that produces the final answer </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lyu et al., 2023</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, and using targeted fine-tuning with causal interventions to ensure the output is robustly grounded in the reasoning steps </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Paul et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Swaroop et al., 2025</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
However, on the whole, strategies that yield robust or generalizable improvements in faithfulness are currently lacking </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">Tanneru et al., 2024</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Training Strategies Against Reward Hacking:</h5>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">Reward hacking is a classical AI Safety problem </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Skalse et al., 2022</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
There is a long history of works in traditional (non-LLM based) reinforcement learning that develop regularizes to prevent policies from converging to undesirable reward hacking based solutions.
For example, impact regularizers </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Armstrong &amp; Levinstein, 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">Turner et al., 2020</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.9" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, frame properties </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.10" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shah et al., 2019</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.12" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.13" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">, human data </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.14" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Carroll et al., 2019</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.16" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.17" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> and constraints  </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.18" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Malik et al., 2021</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.20" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1.21" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
Our proposed MI reward can be viewed through a similar prism as a regularizer term that prevents the reward hacking solution of performing CoT obfuscation and generating some sort of shortcut solution (e.g., generating hacky code), and pushes policy towards a more desired solution of writing code that genuinely solves the given problem.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">In reinforcement learning for LLMs, reward hacking has so far been primarily studied in the context of overoptimization of reward models </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep"><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">(</span><a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gao et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Coste et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Miao et al., 2024</a><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">)</span></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">.
</span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Farquhar et al. (2025)</a></cite><span id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"> study multi-turn reward hacking within LLMs and propose myopic optimization as a potential solution to such reward hacking.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>LLM Usage</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="--ltx-fg-color:#000000;">We used LLMs to aid in writing and in coding of the experiments.
In writing, LLMs were used for typesetting proofs and for sometimes brainstorming what form or way of presenting the content would be optimal.</span></p>
</div>
</section>
</article>
